guide.summary: Mosques, palaces, mangroves and a falcon hospital, with breakfast cafés, Emirati and MICHELIN-starred dinners and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Pre-book your Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque access pass and plan around Fridays, when the mosque pauses visits at midday and Qasr Al Hosn and the Cultural Foundation open only from 2:00 PM; Falcon Hospital tours don't run on Saturdays or public holidays.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.value: Saturday tours off; Friday mornings limited
toolkit.copy: Abu Dhabi Falcon Hospital tours run daily except Saturday and public holidays, according to its tour page (last updated 2018). On Fridays, Qasr Al Hosn and the Cultural Foundation open 2:00 PM to 8:00 PM, and the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque breaks at midday and resumes visits at 2:30 PM.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.value: Pre-book the mosque and falcon tours
toolkit.copy: The Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque asks visitors to pre-book an online access pass, and Abu Dhabi Falcon Hospital says all tours have to be booked in advance. Qasr Al Watan tickets are dated and valid only on the date printed.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins
toolkit.copy: Zuma Abu Dhabi says reservations are not necessary for its counters. Hakkasan Abu Dhabi, Erth and Coya Abu Dhabi take bookings through their own sites or phone lines.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: Qasr Al Watan asks you to cover knees and shoulders and bars shorts, sleeveless tops and see-through garments; Trader Vic's and Buddha-Bar Beach list a smart-casual dress code. At Jubail Mangrove Park bags are security-checked and under-18s must be with an adult.

guide.dek: Plan your sightseeing around Friday hours, pre-book the mosque and the falcon hospital, and save evenings for Al Maryah Island, Saadiyat and the Corniche.
intro: Start with the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, where the Centre's site asks you to pre-book and obtain an online access pass; worshippers may enter directly without a ticket. Its visiting-hours pages show a Friday midday break, with visits resuming at 2:30 PM. Qasr Al Watan, in Al Ras Al Akhdar near the Corniche, sells dated tickets valid only on the printed date and asks you to cover knees and shoulders. Downtown, Qasr Al Hosn's current site lists Saturday to Thursday 9:00 AM to 8:00 PM and Friday 2:00 PM to 8:00 PM, and the Cultural Foundation opposite publishes the same pattern.

For a change of pace, Jubail Mangrove Park on Jubail Island runs guided kayak tours: a 1.5-hour sunrise tour in single or double sit-on-top kayaks and a one-hour single-kayak tour, booked through the park's activities shop. Bags are subject to security checks and under-18s must be accompanied by an adult. Abu Dhabi Falcon Hospital in Al Shamkha offers tours that must be booked in advance; its tour page, last updated in 2018, says they run daily except Saturday and public holidays. On Al Maryah Island, The Galleria opens 10:00 AM to 10:00 PM Sunday to Thursday and until midnight on Friday and Saturday.

Erth in Al Hosn says it retained one MICHELIN star in the 2026 Abu Dhabi guide, and Hakkasan at Emirates Palace Mandarin Oriental lists a 2026 MICHELIN star, with dinner from 6pm every night and lunch on Saturdays. Zuma on Al Maryah Island notes that reservations are not necessary for its counters. Al Fanar at Yas Mall, near Ferrari World, serves Emirati food from 9:00 AM to 10:00 PM daily. For cheaper meals, Shake Shack at Yas Mall and Pickl at Mamsha Soul Beach both list late closing times on their store pages.

Mornings are easy: Jones the Grocer at Garden Plaza, Al Raha opens daily at 8:00am and serves breakfast until 12 pm on weekdays and 4 pm on weekends. Ladurée at Abu Dhabi Mall opens at 9:00 AM, and Cartel Coffee Roasters has branches on Arabian Gulf Street in Al Khalidiyah, at Al Qana and in Khalifa City, though it doesn't publish hours. In the evening, Trader Vic's at Beach Rotana lists a smart-casual dress code and a daily 5pm to 6pm happy hour, and Buddha-Bar Beach at The St. Regis Saadiyat Island Resort asks for smart casual too.
summaryCards: Pair a pre-booked Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque visit with Qasr Al Watan, and avoid Friday mornings at the mosque, Qasr Al Hosn and the Cultural Foundation.
Take breakfast at Jones the Grocer in Al Raha, served until 12 pm on weekdays, then join a guided kayak tour at Jubail Mangrove Park.
Book Abu Dhabi Falcon Hospital tours ahead for any day except Saturday or a public holiday, and dress for Qasr Al Watan with knees and shoulders covered.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Louvre Abu Dhabi, Zayed National Museum, Natural History Museum Abu Dhabi, Four Seasons, Conrad Etihad Towers, Shangri-La, Café Bateel and the World Trade Center Souk returned HTTP 403; Manarat Al Saadiyat and Brioche Dorée had certificate errors; % Arabica returned 418; teamLab Phenomena, Abrahamic Family House, Meylas and Emirates Park Zoo returned empty pages; Wahat Al Karama refused the connection. No market or food hall could be confirmed. Ferrari World, Warner Bros. World, SeaWorld and Yas Waterworld appear to be operating but publish no exact address or hours, so they were left out. The Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque's two official hours pages disagree on closing times; Erth and Jubail Mangrove Park show conflicting hours on their own pages; Ladurée (Abu Dhabi Mall) gives both Level 1 and ground floor. Hours for Cartel Coffee Roasters, Coya Abu Dhabi and Qasr Al Watan are not published, and hours for Tashas, 99 Sushi Bar, Buddha-Bar Beach, Ladurée (Yas Mall), the Cultural Foundation and the Falcon Hospital (page last updated 2018) come from undated or older pages. The bakery picks are patisserie-cafés; no bakery-only operator site could be read.
